items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Lily and I went to visit some friends in Zurich for three days. A certain Mr and Mrs. Harry Pfister.

ctx.x: We finished the Hungaria-Esquire the 31st of March, and that was the end of that orchestra. But Lilly was preparing another tour for the coming autumn and Benny Waters was going to be included in this tour. We had also landed a return engagement for the Esquire in June and had a contract for the month of August at the Caveau Majestic in Blankenberge, Belgium, where I had been refused a permit to work the summer before.

Lily and I went to visit some friends in Zurich for three days. A certain Mr and Mrs. Harry Pfister. Harry played sax and was an arranger also. I had met his wife Bettina in Paris when she came there with Felix Debrit for the jazz festival in 1949, and Felix talked to me about leading a band in Chikito. After the visit with the Pfisters, we went to visit Felix in his country home near Bern for three days and came to Paris the 8th of April.

I assisted in one of the post picturesque weddings I had ever seen. This happened in a part of Paris known as the Commune libre de la Butte Montmarte which is the surrounding of the famous Sacred Heart Church (Sacré Coeur). The marriage was that of a well known Gipsy Violinist Roman Jacowlew to a Miss Pilar Gonzales, a spanish actress.
